'''Efisio Arru''' ([[Siligo]], 1927 – [[Sassari]], 2000) was an Italian scientist, from [[Sardinia]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.comunesiligo.it/siligo/risorse/cittadini/e_arru_ricordo.doc|title=Ricordo di Efisio Arru|trans-title=Remembering Efisio Arru|first=Giovanni|last=Garippa|publisher=Comune di Siligo|language=Italian|year=2005|access-date=2012-10-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072410/http://www.comunesiligo.it/siligo/risorse/cittadini/e_arru_ricordo.doc|archive-date=2016-03-04|url-status=dead}}.</ref> He graduated from the  Veterinary Faculty of the [[University of Sassari]] in 1957, and in 1978 was appointed Professor of Parasitology at that university.  Efisio Arru played a role in the study of parasitology in Italy,<ref>{{citation|first=C.|last=Urbani|title=Le malattie dimenticate. Poesia e lavoro di un medico in prima linea|location=Milano|year=2004|isbn=88-07-17095-7|trans-title=Neglected diseases: poetry and work of a doctor at the front lines|page=179|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tg9lU9Kjs88C&pg=PA179|language=Italian}}.</ref> in particular the study and the fight against   [[Echinococcus]].
